blocks.path: Varicose veins
s: Varicose veins are swollen, twisted veins under the skin, usually on the legs.
They're common and are not usually serious, but there are treatments that can help if they're causing problems.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: Varicose veins are widened veins that look swollen and twisted under the skin.
They may feel lumpy and bulge out.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: They're most common on the legs, but you can get them on other parts of your body.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: They sometimes cause other symptoms that affect your legs, such as:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: pain, aching or a feeling of heaviness

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: skin changes, such as itching, colour changes or dry, scaly skin

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: swollen ankles or legs

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: The symptoms may be worse after standing for a long time, and may get better when you rest with your legs up.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: Varicose veins may get worse without treatment, but this usually happens very slowly over several years.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Check if you have varicose veins
s: They are different from spider veins or thread veins – small red, blue or purple veins that are usually harmless.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Things you can do to help with varicose veins
s: If you have varicose veins, there are things you can do to help with the symptoms.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Things you can do to help with varicose veins > Do try to keep to a healthy weight put your legs up when possible – for example, lie down with your legs on cushions exercise regularly, such as running or walking, to improve blood flow use a moisturising cream or lotion if you have dry, flaky or itchy skin try not to injure your legs, to help prevent bleeding Don’t
s: do not stand for long periods

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Things you can do to help with varicose veins > Do try to keep to a healthy weight put your legs up when possible – for example, lie down with your legs on cushions exercise regularly, such as running or walking, to improve blood flow use a moisturising cream or lotion if you have dry, flaky or itchy skin try not to injure your legs, to help prevent bleeding Don’t
s: do not sit for long periods, unless your feet are raised

s: do not smoke, as it damages your veins – get help to quit smoking

blocks.path: Varicose veins > When and where to get medical help
s: Varicose veins are not usually serious, but sometimes you may need medical help.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > When and where to get medical help > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: You have varicose veins and:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > When and where to get medical help > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you have symptoms such as pain, itching or swelling in your legs

blocks.path: Varicose veins > When and where to get medical help > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: you get a sore on your leg that has not healed after 2 weeks

blocks.path: Varicose veins > When and where to get medical help > Non-urgent advice: See a GP if:
s: they are getting worse

blocks.path: Varicose veins > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: you have varicose veins that are bleeding

blocks.path: Varicose veins > When and where to get medical help > Urgent advice: Ask for an urgent GP appointment or get help from NHS 111 if:
s: You can call 111 or get help from 111 online.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins
s: Varicose veins do not always need treatment.
A GP may refer you to a specialist for tests and treatment if you have:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins
s: symptoms such as pain, heaviness, swollen legs, itching or skin changes

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins
s: any complications, such as ulcers on your legs

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins
s: Treatment to improve how varicose veins look is not usually available on the NHS if they're not causing any other problems.
You may be able to pay for it privately.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: If you're referred to a specialist they'll usually do a test called duplex ultrasound to confirm if you have varicose veins and plan your treatment.
This is a type of scan to check your blood flow.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: There are several types of treatment that may be offered, including:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: procedures to block blood flow in the veins, such as endothermal ablation and foam sclerotherapy

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: surgery to remove varicose veins

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: compression stockings

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The specialist will explain which treatment may be best for you, and the benefits and risks.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: Endothermal ablation

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: This is usually the first choice of treatment for varicose veins.
It works by blocking blood flow in the veins, so they become less swollen.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The main steps are:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll usually be awake during the procedure.
You'll have a local anaesthetic, so you will not feel any pain.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: A thin tube called a catheter is passed up your vein, from a small cut at your ankle or knee.
An ultrasound scan is used to place the catheter.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: A device is put through the catheter and energy from radio waves (radiofrequency ablation) or a laser (endovenous laser treatment) is used to heat the vein that's causing your symptoms.
This closes it off, so that blood stops flowing through it.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The catheter is slowly removed.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll have the procedure in a hospital or clinic.
You'll be able to go home the same day.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You may need to wear compression stockings for about a week.
You may have some pain and bruising, but you should be able to go back to most of your usual activities straight away.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: Foam sclerotherapy

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll usually be offered foam sclerotherapy if endothermal ablation is not suitable for you.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The main steps are:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll be awake during the procedure.
You'll have a local anaesthetic, so you will not feel any pain.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll have injections into your vein of a chemical mixed with air (foam).
An ultrasound scan is used to make sure the injections are in the right place.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The chemical blocks the vein, so that blood stops flowing through it.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll have the procedure in a hospital or clinic.
You'll be able to go home the same day.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You may need to wear compression stockings for about a week.
You may have some pain and bruising, but you should be able to go back to most of your usual activities straight away.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: Surgery to remove varicose veins (ligation and stripping)

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You may be offered surgery to remove varicose veins, called ligation and stripping, if simpler procedures are not suitable for you.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The main steps are:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The surgeon will mark your legs to show where the vein needs to be removed.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll usually be asleep during the operation.
You'll have a general anaesthetic, so you will not feel any pain.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The surgeon makes 1 cut in your upper leg (groin) and a 2nd cut lower down your leg, at your knee or ankle.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The surgeon finds the vein through the 1st cut and ties it, to stop blood flowing.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: A thin, flexible wire is passed down the vein to the 2nd cut.
The surgeon uses the wire to pull the vein out.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: The cuts are closed using stitches that dissolve so they do not need to be removed.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You can usually go home the same day.
Moving around may be uncomfortable for a few days, and you may have some pain and bruising for a few weeks.
You may need to take 1 to 2 weeks off work.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: Your leg will be tightly bandaged or you'll need to wear compression stockings for about a week.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: Compression stockings

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: Compression stockings work by putting pressure on your lower legs.
This improves your blood flow and can help with swelling and pain.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: You'll only be offered compression stockings for varicose veins if procedures or surgery are not suitable for you, or if you do not need other treatments.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: They're not suitable if you have problems with blood flow in your arteries.
A specialist can check for this.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: There are different types of stockings, and it's important to talk to a doctor or pharmacist to make sure you get the right type for you.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Assessment and treatment from a specialist
s: It's best to wear them during the day and remove them at bedtime.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Treating varicose veins in pregnancy
s: If you get varicose veins during pregnancy, you may be able to use compression stockings, but procedures or surgery to treat them are not usually recommended while you're pregnant.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Treatment for varicose veins > Treating varicose veins in pregnancy
s: Varicose veins often get better or go away after your baby's born.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: Varicose veins happen when the valves that control the flow of blood in your vein do not work properly.
This causes blood to build up and put pressure on the vein, which makes it swell and twist.

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: Varicose veins are very common and anyone can get them, but it's more likely to happen if you:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: are a woman

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: are older

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: are overweight

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: are pregnant

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: spend a lot of time standing or sitting

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: have other family members with varicose veins

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Causes of varicose veins
s: have had deep vein thrombosis (DVT)

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Complications of varicose veins
s: Varicose veins do not usually cause any serious problems.
But they can sometimes cause complications including:

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Complications of varicose veins
s: bleeding

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Complications of varicose veins
s: itchy, flaky, dry skin over your veins (varicose eczema)

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Complications of varicose veins
s: sores that take a long time to heal (venous leg ulcers)

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Complications of varicose veins
s: blood clots under your skin that cause hard, painful veins (superficial vein thrombosis)

blocks.path: Varicose veins > Complications of varicose veins
s: blood clots deeper inside your leg (deep vein thrombosis – DVT)
